[Watch original](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3axY1wz2OvA) · [Transcript lines](https://github.com/flaviusapop/ai-engineer-evals/blob/main/transcripts/3axY1wz2OvA.md#L197-L199)

## Managing production retrieval, data and provenance

Manage retrieval configuration, exact document and inventory access, and source provenance, including governed trace-data storage and document evidence pipelines. Trace instrumentation, interpretation and incident triage belong to the observability guide; retrieval optimization is covered separately.

A retrieval system must do more than find plausible text. It must make the right evidence available, preserve where each assertion came from, and distinguish search results from complete, current records. These are different responsibilities: an auditable citation or deterministic query does not by itself prove that a source or answer is correct.

## Prepare and maintain candidate indexes

Different signals call for different indexes. An illustrative video corpus might maintain an inverted topic index, a graph of entities and a vector index for visual similarity. Offline processing extracts and clusters content; refresh jobs update those representations as the corpus changes. Online, query metadata chooses candidate types, quality filters remove obvious spam, and a ranking stage selects what to inspect. This is an architecture example, not evidence for a particular refresh interval or performance gain. For how lexical and semantic result lists are combined, see [Retrieval and query optimization](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/retrieval-and-query-optimization.html). [Source 1](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-1)

Bind an embedding model and its configuration to the indexed field so document ingestion and query embedding use the same model rather than relying on every caller to remember it. A change of model needs a coordinated index migration; the cited guidance does not establish a method for aligning different models or require inference inside the database. [Source 2](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-2)

Static routing selects a predefined search template for a query. It is not the same as a feedback system that changes weights or filters based on clicks, ratings and business outcomes. One workshop described the latter as a possible future capability and explicitly said it had not been released. [Source 3](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-3)

## Select evidence and make it inspectable

If the answer model sees only a few chunks, evaluate the actual window it receives: the relevant passage at rank 20 cannot help if only three are passed through. Adding many plausible but conflicting passages can also make selection harder. An alternative proposal stages titles and snippets in a workspace and lets an agent open selected documents; it is not an independently validated optimal context strategy. [Source 4](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-4) [Source 5](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-5)

Pass source URLs and document metadata with retrieved text rather than asking the generator to invent links. For numerical work, a stronger design registers stable fact identities and preserves the source, transformation and displayed value separately. A number displayed in thousands can then be traced back to its underlying fact and calculation. One financial platform reports such a registry and clickable calculations; its repeatability and universal clickability are speaker-reported, not independently tested. A basic URL-bearing demonstration is a different, weaker mechanism. Neither verifies that the cited passage entails the claim or that the source itself is true. [Source 6](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-6) [Source 7](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-7)

When a number cannot be matched to a registered fact, remove or abstain from the unsupported claim, or attempt a separately checked repair before accepting it. The cited platform describes selective repair but does not disclose its acceptance criteria or accuracy; it is not evidence that an arbitrary repair is trustworthy. [Source 8](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-8)

Relevance is not authority. A filing and an earnings call can disagree about a metric; compare reporting period, definition and restatement before deciding which source answers the question, and expose unresolved conflict. For implemented software behavior, code may outrank stale documentation, while documentation can explain intended behavior. That ranking is task-specific, not a universal rule; a reported code/document integration was still being fixed. [Source 9](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-9) [Source 10](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-10)

## Navigate documents and query exact state

Search snippets are a starting point, not proof of completeness. For linked rulebooks, provide ordered-section access, a bounded whole-document read and a list of available documents so the agent can follow cross-references or investigate an exhaustive fee request. If a document is too large or a section name invalid, return available sections rather than silently truncating. One deployment used an approximately 100,000-token whole-document limit; that is its guardrail, not a general optimum, and these tools alone do not prove every fee was found. [Source 11](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-11) [Source 12](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-12)

Separate volatile state from relatively stable preferences. Refresh inventory before recommending an item whose availability matters; the source does not give a universal freshness window. [Source 13](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-13)

For exhaustive structured inventory, let the model interpret the request and let code enumerate records. In the reported example, “hot GPUs in data hall 11” becomes an entity type, a location subtree and a temperature predicate; the backend intersects the matching sets. A naming pattern can similarly be generated and executed against actual identifiers. Sharding a list across model calls had produced both missing and invented equipment. Exact set operations still depend on the correct interpretation, complete inventory and correctly specified “hot” filter; reported zero failures on 66 cases do not establish universal end-to-end reliability. [Source 14](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-14) [Source 15](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-15) [Source 16](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-16) [Source 17](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-17) [Source 18](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-18)

## Preserve lineage in domain workflows

A provenance chain should connect external and internal documents, extracted facts, derived values and model-directed input/output operations. For example, an *illustrative* business ratio should link both input versions and the calculation to the result, not merely link a public filing. This makes reconstruction possible; it does not certify the inputs or arithmetic. The cited account does not supply a complete ledger schema or retention policy. [Source 19](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-19)

At intake, detect repeat submissions without erasing their individual histories. Delays can cause follow-ups that increase review load and falsely look like independent corroboration; an altered date may instead warrant separate investigation. Duplicate rates in the example are illustrative. [Source 20](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-20)

Research workflows can combine analyst notes, expert-call material and alternative datasets, then surface a shelved thesis when market conditions change. A proposed workbench presents recommendations with exact evidence and saves the human–agent synthesis back into the research corpus. Treat saved synthesis as another reviewable claim, not an authoritative source merely because it is retained. Neither proposal establishes better investment performance. [Source 21](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-21) [Source 22](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-22) [Source 23](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-23)

Similarly, attach error rates and instrumentation gaps to a software migration target so an agent can address why the migration was undertaken, not just translate syntax. Measure the stated operational goal alongside conversion; the telemetry-enriched migration is a proposed extension, not a demonstrated improvement. [Source 24](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-24)

## Operate trace and document data

Treat traces as governed, text-rich data: define a shared schema and access for audit, operational monitoring, interactive reading and programmatic analysis across frameworks. Text indexing can support searches across spans; choose storage for actual workload and access constraints rather than assuming a custom database is required. The large span sizes described by a vendor are examples, not typical measurements. For interpreting traces, see [Tracing and diagnosing production behavior](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-observability-and-diagnosis.html). [Source 25](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-25) [Source 26](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-26) [Source 27](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-27)

For recurring document work, a specialized pipeline may be appropriate: classify and split mixed packets, parse, retrieve, extract fields and format outputs. Check each stage and the end-to-end result against representative live inputs: a split that hides a page can undermine otherwise accurate extraction. Attach field-level source references and uncertainty flags for review; a confidence score is not necessarily calibrated. The sources offer operational guidance, not quantified improvements. [Source 28](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-28) [Source 29](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-29) [Source 30](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-30) [Source 31](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-31)

Connected dependency data can also support ecosystem review: a demonstration generated an architecture report flagging cycles, migration issues, single points of failure and telemetry gaps. Treat those findings as leads to verify, not an independently validated audit; no precision measurement was given. [Source 32](#retrieval-evidence-and-provenance-source-32)

## Delivering agent-assisted work with human review

Owns software-delivery practices and adoption; runtime controls and evaluation infrastructure are separate. Review capacity, decisions and handoffs rather than test-suite construction.

An agent can produce a change faster than a team can decide whether it should exist, understand it, or release it. A workable delivery process therefore starts with intent and ends with an accountable decision—not with a generated pull request. Adapt the amount of automation and review to the project, the evidence available, and the consequences of being wrong.

## Adapt the workflow to the project

A harness demonstrated on a new application may assume a particular stack, design system and set of checks. In an established repository, test it against the actual build, conventions and change constraints before expanding its remit. Starting with monitoring, issue creation and reviewable pull requests can be more appropriate than handing over whole-application generation. The cited greenfield pattern was not validated as a long-lived brownfield deployment. Its speakers favored reducing recurring human intervention, while audience members wanted sprint reviews; stop-and-resume hooks are a proposed alternative, not a settled answer for every project. [Source 1](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-1) [Source 2](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-2)

Invite skeptical maintainers to identify what generated changes routinely miss: undocumented dependencies, project conventions, or tests that cannot expose a particular regression. Give them ownership of a roadmap to close those gaps rather than treating their reluctance as an adoption problem. They may already be absorbing the integration burden created by faster generation. This is organizational experience and advice, not evidence that the approach caused adoption to rise. [Source 3](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-3) [Source 4](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-4)

## Decide what to build before delegating

Start the brief with the user problem and why the change matters. Investigate the current system and ask only clarification questions whose answers could change the work. A reviewed plan records the intended behavior, constraints, proposed scope and unresolved decisions so that implementation can proceed without losing the purpose. One team describes substantial up-front planning; that is a local practice, not a required duration. A separate experiment reported improved repeatability from targeted clarification across tested agents, but did not establish a universal prompt or guarantee. [Source 5](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-5) [Source 6](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-6) [Source 7](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-7)

When no specification exists, observe the work. In a hypothetical document-exception assistant, shadow an analyst to learn which systems are consulted, where judgment and permission enter, and what happens when a document is missing. Draft a workflow naming accessible documents, permitted processing, output, reviewer and submitter; take it to sponsors and control owners for correction. Agree on success against the current process rather than inventing a precise error target from the source's garbled caption. [Source 8](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-8)

Choose the smallest useful increment with a credible approval path. Summarizing material an analyst already holds, reading a second system, drafting customer-facing text and sending it automatically are different scopes with different review questions. Existing access does not automatically authorize a new use, and small scope is not an exemption from controls. [Source 9](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-9)

## Make work reviewable and keep it steerable

Record the work on shared, durable surfaces: an issue describes the request, an agent run produces a pull request, and reviewers leave corrections on that change. Versioned team workflows make later inspection and improvement possible; visibility alone is neither proof of safe automation nor permission to disclose the record publicly. A low-friction way to introduce agents is to ask for a bounded task in an existing team conversation and have the agent report back in the same thread. The cited organization still had unresolved build-system dependencies for cloud agents. [Source 10](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-10) [Source 11](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-11)

Label agent-written changes and distinguish a short human-authored explanation of intent from generated supporting detail. This is a useful local convention, not a universal compliance rule. The initiating person remains responsible for the handoff and remediation. Tests, logs and review artifacts are evidence; an accountable person or organization still decides whether to ship, block, or accept risk. An automatically triggered first draft does not itself have authority to merge. The responsible owner should be able to explain the intent, evidence and risks without necessarily reading or typing every line; human approval itself is not proof of safety. [Source 12](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-12) [Source 13](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-13) [Source 14](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-14) [Source 15](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-15) [Source 16](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-16)

For long or parallel workstreams, maintain checkpoints and evidence as work progresses rather than asking a reviewer to reconstruct a day of decisions from a final summary. A green test suite can coexist with a growing gap between the code in the system and what the team understands. Review needs to preserve comprehension as well as find defects. [Source 17](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-17) [Source 18](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-18)

Give each consumer a usable review surface: humans need readable findings, rationale and links to the rules applied; an agent revising the work needs structured findings and repair context. A proposed alternative groups changes around intent and demonstrated outcomes, such as a feature video. It may conserve attention, but a video or automated review can miss hidden implementation defects; neither approach has demonstrated equivalent defect detection in the cited material. Use potential blast radius to prioritize review, not as a proven threshold for bypassing it. [Source 19](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-19) [Source 20](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-20) [Source 21](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-21)

When multiple automated loops make PRs, route a designated review comment, the diff and relevant discussion only to the loop responsible for that PR. Labels can support routing; they do not by themselves authorize comments or defend against malicious instructions. Review approvals and revision requests can also become feedback for improving the workflow, subject to human interpretation. Return classified developer replies, action rates and traces to the teams that own local review rules so they can revise unhelpful ones. Addressing a comment or expressing sentiment is not independent proof that a finding was correct. [Source 22](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-22) [Source 23](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-23) [Source 24](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-24) [Source 25](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-25) [Source 26](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-26)

Keep operational intervention possible as well: a research interface can allow people to cancel or add experiments, inspect links between ideas and outcomes, and receive escalation on failure. Telemetry-informed self-correction is a proposal, not evidence of a safe action policy. If a conversation is converted into proposed product changes, ground it in the relevant application and let the user review before applying. One wearable demonstration used preloaded data; a repository-aware backlog integration was unfinished, so neither establishes reliable autonomous backlog creation. [Source 27](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-27) [Source 28](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-28) [Source 29](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-29) [Source 30](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-30) [Source 31](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-31)

## Shorten feedback without confusing it with verification

A quick prototype can support a product conversation even when its code is disposable. For a desktop product, one team created a web shell and per-PR preview links so colleagues could inspect variants without each installing a local build. That offers a faster shared feedback surface, but it does not establish coverage of native desktop behavior. Reusable accessible components can similarly make a fix available in several places; each use still needs contextual accessibility verification. [Source 32](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-32) [Source 33](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-33) [Source 34](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-34)

Layer verification: provide project guidance before generation, give the agent feedback during implementation, use CI checks before integration, and maintain the codebase after delivery. These layers address different opportunities to prevent, detect and repair problems; installing a set of tools is not proof that they work. Embedding governance in a harness is a proposed architecture, not demonstrated compliance. For the detailed mechanics of gates see [Building verification feedback and integration gates](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-feedback-loops-and-integration-gates.html); for enforcement of authority see [Agent Authority, Isolation and Runtime Controls](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-authority-isolation-and-runtime-controls.html). [Source 35](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-35) [Source 36](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-36)

After preview and approval, observe the deployed behavior. VS Code describes staged releases monitored through errors and issues, particularly useful when rolling back installed software is costly. A separate agent-watched rollout is an emerging proposal. Neither account supplies a validated abort threshold or measured incident reduction; decide in advance who can react and how. [Source 37](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-37) [Source 38](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-38)

Operational failures can feed reviewed changes: filter and group related error stacks into owned issues, let an agent investigate and propose a fix, and provide a way for people to correct mistaken triage. One reported VS Code pipeline follows this pattern. A proposed voice-agent loop would replay failed traces against a development fix and present the result for approval; it was imagined future work, not a completed autonomous repair experiment. [Source 39](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-39) [Source 40](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-40) [Source 41](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-41)

## Measure the delivery system, not just generation

Faster code production can move the queue into design, review, testing, security or recovery. Track the flow from user feedback through decision, validation, release and learning, including the burden on reviewers. A code-review vendor reported widely varying PR throughput among its users, but more PRs do not establish more useful or safe functionality. [Source 42](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-42) [Source 43](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-43) [Source 44](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-44)

Treat activity measures as proxies. Committed agent-written code measures acceptance, not correctness; a reported increase coincided with model and harness changes. Inferred authorship depends on labeling and the vendor's customer mix. Review rounds depend on task scope and reviewer behavior; the captioned numerical comparison is corrupted. Addressed comments measure action, and unreviewed merges measure adoption of a workflow—not safe outcomes. Compare these signals with independently observed defects and product outcomes rather than treating any one as a quality verdict. [Source 45](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-45) [Source 46](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-46) [Source 47](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-47) [Source 48](#planning-and-delivering-agent-assisted-software-source-48)

## Voice-agent operations

Owns audio timing, conversational concurrency and voice telemetry; generic tracing belongs elsewhere.

A voice agent has to keep the conversation usable while it waits for systems that may be slow, interpret whether a pause means the caller is finished, and preserve enough audio and action context to explain what actually happened. A fluent response alone proves neither that the caller finished speaking nor that a backend action succeeded.

## Keep the microphone available during slow work

A booking or lookup can take seconds or tens of seconds. Rather than block the conversational thread until the tool returns, a tool can yield an initial update, letting the agent acknowledge the request, listen and collect other information while the operation continues. In a narrated hotel demonstration, saves proceed while the agent asks for subsequent booking details. One presenter suggests considering asynchronous handling for operations over one second; treat that as a design heuristic, not a universal threshold. [Source 1](#voice-agent-operations-source-1) [Source 2](#voice-agent-operations-source-2)

The operational distinction is between **pending** and **completed**. An acknowledgment such as “I’m checking that” can be truthful while “your reservation is confirmed” is not yet justified. If a tool returns an error, the agent needs a way to correct the record, retry where appropriate or hand off to a person. If the caller revises a request while a save is in flight, the implementation also needs an explicit approach to cancellation, stale results and consistency before claiming that the final state matches the conversation. The demonstrations do not establish those mechanisms, and the error recovery was narrated rather than demonstrated with a failed call. [Source 2](#voice-agent-operations-source-2) [Source 1](#voice-agent-operations-source-1)

## Treat a pause as evidence, not a full stop

A silence threshold plus a transcript can mistake a pause inside an utterance for the end of a turn. Rhythm, pitch and intonation provide additional information about whether the speaker intends to continue. In the speaker’s payment example, a pause after “500” precedes completion of the amount as 555.23. Cutting in at the pause could change what the agent believes was authorized. This is an illustration of the mechanism, not a measured comparison establishing that every acoustically informed detector is superior. [Source 3](#voice-agent-operations-source-3)

Test both sides of the decision: an incomplete amount or sentence followed by a meaningful pause, and a genuinely completed turn where excessive waiting would be awkward. Include interruptions and listen to the actual audio, not only the final transcription. For the separate question of measuring when the agent becomes audible, see [Interactive latency](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/interactive-latency.html).

## Connect the score to the call

A list of isolated events cannot by itself show how an interruption, a tool call and a spoken response interacted. Stitch the call together with a session identifier and speaker tags; preserve the sequence of turns, playable audio, transcript, timing, pauses, cutoffs, tool inputs and outputs. A suspicious evaluation score should link to the particular audio span it evaluates and to the surrounding interaction, so a reviewer can hear what happened and inspect the action made at that time. The described interface presents these connections; its debugging advantage was not independently compared against alternatives. [Source 4](#voice-agent-operations-source-4) [Source 5](#voice-agent-operations-source-5) [Source 6](#voice-agent-operations-source-6)

For example, a weather lookup aligned with the session audio provides a way to examine whether a tool problem coincided with the caller speaking over the agent, rather than attributing a bad answer to the tool on the basis of timing-free logs alone. A score can trigger further investigation, but the described automatic workflows have no reported precision, incident-reduction or safety evaluation. [Source 5](#voice-agent-operations-source-5) [Source 6](#voice-agent-operations-source-6)

The same source imagines a more ambitious future loop: diagnose oversized tool results, try truncation in development, replay failed traces against that endpoint, and present latency evidence in a pull request for human approval. That is a proposed verification workflow, **not** a demonstrated autonomous repair system. Successful replay would still need to examine whether truncation removed information needed for correct responses. [Source 7](#voice-agent-operations-source-7) For selecting production cases as durable evaluation material, see [Build and maintain production-grounded evaluation sets](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/build-and-maintain-production-grounded-evaluation-sets.html).

## Normalize events without erasing their meaning

Different voice providers expose different event shapes and response lifecycles. Map their events into a common queryable schema for sessions, inputs, conversation items, outputs and token counts. This lets an operator ask a comparable question across provider changes without writing each query from scratch. [Source 8](#voice-agent-operations-source-8)

The mapping is useful only when it faithfully captures the events and semantics relevant to the investigation. Check, for example, whether an interruption or output boundary means the same thing in each integration and whether missing events are distinguishable from events that never occurred. A vendor’s assertion of broad coverage and automatic capture is not an interoperability test; retain provider-specific context when a common field would hide a meaningful difference. [Source 8](#voice-agent-operations-source-8)

## Evaluation infrastructure and team ownership

Owns human responsibilities and reusable experimentation infrastructure, not specific monitoring choices. Owns team responsibilities and architectural capacity, not individual launch approvals.

Evaluation is both a shared technical capability and a set of decisions someone must own. A platform can make runs and evidence accessible, but it cannot decide what a particular product should do, supply domain judgment by itself, or make an ambiguous owner accountable.

## Register agent purpose and accountable ownership

Maintain a discoverable inventory recording each agent's product, purpose, accountable owner, tools and endpoints. Someone investigating an unexpected action can then find the responsible team and understand the intended use; another team can discover an existing capability before rebuilding it. Approved development frameworks can populate the registry automatically, with manual registration for agents outside that path. The proposal favors low-friction visibility rather than making every experiment wait in a universal central approval queue, which can encourage invisible shadow IT. It does not provide measured governance outcomes or a risk-scoring formula. [Source 1](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-1) [Source 2](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-2)

A registry is an inventory, not a permission grant or evidence of compliance. Runtime enforcement and risk-sensitive human review are separate responsibilities: see [Agent Authority, Isolation and Runtime Controls](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-authority-isolation-and-runtime-controls.html) and [Human Review and Agent Governance](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/human-review-and-agent-governance.html).

## Share quality work across disciplines

Organize around the user problem rather than assigning an entire agent product to a model team merely because it uses AI. Data scientists contribute testing and risk expertise; product and domain specialists understand the desired behavior; application and systems engineers connect tools, services and interfaces. A supervisor invoking child agents across infrastructure illustrates why model knowledge alone does not specify the surrounding system. This is organizational guidance and an architectural example, not a measured staffing formula. [Source 3](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-3) [Source 4](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-4)

One practical division is for product managers to frame success hypotheses, domain experts to define and label consequential cases, analysts to interpret results, and engineers to implement data integration and automated runs. In DoorDash's account, strategy and operations set priorities and quality bars, product teams develop rubrics and workflows, operations annotate, and engineering supplies APIs and telemetry. These are local choices, not a mandatory organizational chart. Judge-prompt ownership can sit with operations, product or engineering in different teams; the key is to name an owner and make changes reviewable. [Source 5](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-5) [Source 6](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-6) [Source 7](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-7)

**Illustrative handoff:** for an insurance assistant, the product owner identifies a disputed-claim workflow, an insurance expert labels what an acceptable answer must include, and an engineer turns those cases into repeatable runs. The owner reviews disagreements with the expert before changing the rubric. The tooling carries the evidence; the participants remain responsible for its interpretation. Domain participation should not depend on every expert being able to code. [Source 8](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-8)

## Share primitives, keep local decisions close to the work

A central platform team can provide stable APIs for traces, scores and datasets, plus workflow primitives for annotation and judge calibration. Domain teams can then build or use interfaces suited to their own tasks without waiting for a centrally built custom screen for every change. DoorDash describes telemetry and human-workflow surfaces backed by shared APIs, and a self-service calibration interface where product managers or operators can configure a run and choose a judge model. The architecture is a reported case, not a published endpoint contract or a reliability measurement; the ability to run a calibration does not guarantee that an unsupported user has produced a valid judge. [Source 9](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-9) [Source 10](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-10)

A spreadsheet can be a useful starting point. A polished results screen improves access but remains a reporting tool if users cannot change a prompt, model or parameter and compare persisted runs. The next useful capability is to retain configurations and evidence so stakeholders can inspect side-by-side experiments over time. Shared infrastructure need not mean central sign-off for every iteration; conversely, local autonomy does not remove the need for an accountable quality owner. The recommended progression is a design proposal, not a required sequence for every organization. [Source 11](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-11) [Source 2](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-2)

Offline experiment interfaces also do not show what happens after deployment by themselves. For that distinct operational loop, see [Monitoring production quality and improvement](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/production-evaluation-and-monitoring.html).

## Organize accountable development and architecture evolution

Give domain quality a named decision-maker with authority to participate, rather than making experts advisory while no one can resolve a disagreement. One speaker advocates a principal domain expert; this is an opinion informed by a case, not evidence that one reporting structure always wins. Make plans and review requests visible to engineers and product stakeholders so requirements can be corrected before execution finishes. A shared board is a demonstrated collaboration design, not a measured improvement in outcomes. [Source 12](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-12) [Source 13](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-13)

Leaders can prototype, but an interruptible leader should avoid becoming the sole critical-path dependency: meetings and incidents can leave the rest of the team blocked. Assign delivery and review ownership to people with capacity to follow through. [Source 14](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-14)

Start with an architecture proportionate to the risk and reserve capacity to replace parts as needs become clear. One internal assistant reportedly began with long instructions and a simple tool stack, adding CI/CD, evaluation infrastructure and a skill library later. That retrospective is not proof that delaying evaluations or controls is appropriate in a high-risk deployment; a workable early stack still needs risk-appropriate quality gates. [Source 15](#evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership-source-15)

Evidence: case_study. The account is retrospective and vendor-specific; it does not demonstrate that postponing CI or evaluation infrastructure is appropriate for every risk level.

[Watch original](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DrTdD-ttjCY) · [Transcript lines](https://github.com/flaviusapop/ai-engineer-evals/blob/main/transcripts/DrTdD-ttjCY.md#L51-L51)

## Validating model and serving systems

Owns model-serving compatibility, availability and research control rather than task-level agent quality. Model, backend and serving lifecycle rather than user-facing product adoption.

A model that produces acceptable answers in a notebook is not automatically ready to serve real traffic. The model, serving engine, accelerator software, request mix and operational controls form a system. Validate that system on the workload it must run, and keep functional quality separate from speed claims.

## Validate the actual serving stack

First establish that the model, engine, accelerator and software versions work together. An unsupported operation or incompatible engine can look like a model failure, so capture the configuration alongside results. Then exercise realistic input and output lengths, concurrency and traffic patterns, inspecting actual responses as well as response time. Include errors, GPU state, cold starts and recovery under traffic; steady-state generation throughput cannot describe all of the user experience. A reported multi-node recovery illustrates the distinction but supplies neither an availability target nor a measured error budget. [Source 1](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-1) [Source 2](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-2)

The required degree of control depends on the work. A managed endpoint may be adequate when the question is whether a checkpoint serves the workload; research that changes kernels or inference scheduling needs access to the implementation below that endpoint. Portable weights alone do not supply that control. The cited deployment discussion is partly promotional and does not establish a provider’s production performance. [Source 3](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-3) For detailed performance measurement, see [Measuring inference serving performance](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/inference-serving.html).

## Investigate intermittent corruption by moving the failure

When corruption appears only after many requests, vary one workload or resource dimension at a time and observe how the failure’s timing and location change, not just whether it appears. In one reported incident, reducing GPU memory allocation from 90% to 20% and issuing many concurrent requests made rare gibberish easier to reproduce. The team used temperature zero in that setup; this does not guarantee determinism on every system. [Source 4](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-4)

The same team carried request IDs into the model’s forward context, where individual requests otherwise appeared as anonymous tensors. Inspecting the failing request exposed decode occurring before the expected prefill. In another incident, increasing rollouts per prompt moved a periodic spike earlier, making its connection to workload structure visible. Lower memory allocation helped expose the first problem but hid the second, an overflow involving a smaller reachable buffer. A symptom-free run after a perturbation is therefore a clue to explain, not proof of correctness. These are specific reported incidents, not evidence of prevalence across engines. [Source 5](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-5) [Source 6](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-6) [Source 7](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-7)

## Route for the objective, then test the boundary

Task matching and selection within a model pool are separate decisions. A preferred-order policy sends requests to the chosen model until it fails, then tries an eligible fallback; a fastest policy chooses using recent latency instead. Resilience is a distinct goal from cost or speed, and an alternative must be suitable for the task, not merely reachable. A vendor demo configured both approaches, using a roughly 30-minute latency window for its fastest policy; it did not induce a provider failure or prove that window optimal. [Source 8](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-8) [Source 9](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-9)

Task labels such as “fast” or “finance” can hide changing model identifiers from users, enabling backend swaps or traffic splits. They do not make backends equivalent. Test response schemas, tool calls, error handling and the actual adapter path. For example, structured citation blocks can make attribution easier to render than free-form text, but their structure does not establish factual grounding. A coding-agent bridge may need adaptation to accept a different harness’s requests even when both harnesses can consume the same text instructions. [Source 10](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-10) [Source 11](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-11) [Source 12](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-12)

Hardware portability is another boundary. A layer between device-specific kernels and higher-level inference and deployment can localize accelerator adaptations rather than multiplying changes throughout the stack. It still needs testing on each model and workload, and maximum performance may require device-specific tuning. Broad support in the cited architecture is a vendor claim, not proof that every configuration works. [Source 13](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-13)

## Validate model and system changes together

Compare a replacement model or quantization on local tasks in the actual harness, not only on a leaderboard. Check existing behavior as well as newly available capabilities. A model upgrade might remove the need for an old tool-use workaround, but exploiting it may require changing orchestration; not every swap requires a rewrite. If the system now adds memory, retrieval, tools or code execution, tests inherited from a simpler system cover only part of it. A practitioner’s assessment of quantized models in coding harnesses is qualitative, not a standardized comparative trial. [Source 14](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-14) [Source 15](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-15) [Source 16](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-16) [Source 17](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-17)

One speaker suggests waiting a couple of weeks after a model release unless evaluating new models is part of the job. That is personal timing advice, not an established optimal delay: waiting does not replace local validation. [Source 18](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-18) See [Model selection and runtime efficiency](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/model-selection-and-runtime-efficiency.html) for task-level selection tradeoffs.

## Shape demand and preserve a rollback path

Agent traffic can contain bursts of short-lived branches and retries rather than the predictable warm-cache pattern of a single human session. Ingress shaping and rate limits can bound admitted work; cache-aware compute routing can send work toward useful cached state. These address infrastructure demand, whereas the model-pool policy above chooses a provider or model. The cited architecture is a roadmap without a complete control policy or benchmark, so test its behavior under the actual burst and retry mix. [Source 19](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-19)

Before adopting a faster serving version, check outputs and load behavior on the workload, decide who owns monitoring and incident response, and preserve a way back to the prior version. A provider describes prioritizing quality at initial model launch, followed by a backlog for cache, attention kernels and quantization. Those are reported practices, not measured quality-preservation or speed guarantees; the update guidance does not specify a rollout threshold or demonstrate rollback. [Source 20](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-20) [Source 21](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-21)

## Keep speech integration modular

For speech-to-text, speaker reconciliation can sit in an orchestration layer rather than requiring each transcription model to be retrained. This makes a model replacement an interface test: check how its timestamps and overlapping speech interact with reconciliation. The source presents broad model independence as a plan, not demonstrated compatibility with every speech system. [Source 22](#inference-and-serving-operations-source-22) For the larger interaction context, see [Voice interaction and speech system evaluation](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/voice-interaction-and-speech-system-evaluation.html).

## Managing agent task flow and action evidence

Own task progression, action evidence and handoffs; not general-purpose evaluation metrics or permission policy.

Agent work is not finished merely because a model says it is done. A useful workflow makes it possible to tell who owns the next step, whether the receiving step can use the output, what actually happened at an external boundary, and what evidence supports the outcome. Those are related but distinct questions.

## Separate required gates from adaptive repair

Map the dependencies that must hold before work advances. A proposed design puts those forward dependencies and required gates in an outer workflow, while allowing iteration inside a node: a code-review step can request changes and review again without skipping the later required check. Independent reviews can run in parallel, then join before a dependent decision. In the illustrative lending workflow, some verification and financial work can proceed alongside each other even though later steps remain ordered. This is an architectural proposal, not a proven compiler or measured speedup. [Source 1](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-1) [Source 2](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-2)

A workflow diagram states the intended progression; it does not by itself enforce access restrictions. Policy intent and the running system are different things, and runtime restrictions must actually be implemented. See [Agent Authority, Isolation and Runtime Controls](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-authority-isolation-and-runtime-controls.html) for enforcement. [Source 3](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-3)

## Advance work without losing custody or shared updates

Choose the next task from current state and record its dependencies, allowed transitions, blocker, current owner and next action. When the producer finishes, name the reviewer or other recipient and what they must do; stopping the producer is not the same as transferring custody. One coding-loop practitioner recommends selecting the next important ticket afresh after each change, and, when workers share a backlog, claiming a ticket and checking for contention before starting. His failed parallel attempt is not proof that parallel work is generally impossible. Ticket claims alone are not atomic locks. [Source 4](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-4) [Source 5](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-5) [Source 6](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-6) [Source 7](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-7)

A watchdog can notice stalled progress and prompt further work, but it must respect genuine blockers and a bounded stopping rule: activity is not evidence of completion. The described watchdog and liveness invariants are proposals, not guarantees of termination. [Source 8](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-8) [Source 9](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-9)

Coordination also applies to data, not only tickets. Two workers can read the same old state, independently edit it, and have the second save erase the first. Order commits at each shared mutable boundary with a suitable transaction, queue or lock; independent reads and unrelated work need not be serialized. This is a proposed invariant, not a tested universal locking implementation. [Source 10](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-10) For topology choices, see [Choosing agent delegation and coordination](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-delegation-and-coordination.html).

## Accept the artifact, not just the handoff

Custody says who acts next. An artifact contract says what the receiver needs. Check required fields and structure at the producer-consumer boundary, then check substantive domain requirements before promotion. After changing a prompt or skill, rerun representative downstream checks: a locally plausible artifact may break several consumers. This delivery-control inventory comes from one practitioner's workflow, not a framework comparison. [Source 11](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-11) [Source 12](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-12) [Source 13](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-13)

A content demonstration makes the distinction concrete: a complete, ready-marked package can still have an opening hook that repeats a previous angle. Compare that meaningful unit against relevant history rather than merely checking that the file is new. The demonstration does not disclose a similarity algorithm or threshold; novelty is one domain gate, not a substitute for the rest of the contract. [Source 14](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-14)

## Observe current state and validate recovery

Before choosing an action, refresh the facts the step can actually access: workflow position, current components and errors, and relevant operational measurements. One reported pipeline snapshot returns flow context and specific error codes, helping an agent refer to present components rather than remembered names. It comes with no stated consistency or concurrent-edit guarantee. Check for missing or inaccessible context rather than assuming the snapshot is complete; keep a human-readable operational view as well as programmatic access. Dynamic feedback can guide the next step, but changing output is different from cacheable static instructions. [Source 15](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-15) [Source 16](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-16) [Source 17](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-17) [Source 18](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-18)

For remediation, distinguish **proposal → permission → executor capability → attempt → verified recovery**. A bounded set of actions makes a decision inspectable, but a safe proposed action is not necessarily available, and an available action is not necessarily successful. In a synthetic incident capstone, a datetime conversion is reportedly permitted but unavailable in the executor; the incident is recorded and sent for manual review rather than called fixed. The captions are corrupted, so this interpretation is provisional; it is not evidence of live recovery. If an action is attempted, check the actual downstream result, such as a successful rerun and the resulting data, before reporting recovery. A fixed decision threshold is a teaching simplification, not an established production policy. [Source 19](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-19) [Source 20](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-20) [Source 21](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-21) [Source 22](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-22)

## Time checks to the recovery window

Inspect arguments and results before or during consequential actions when waiting would make errors unsafe or hard to reverse. A vendor describes selected appointment checks that can run after a call if an error can still be corrected or a patient called back. That example does not make urgent clinical risks deferrable, nor does a later check guarantee correctness. [Source 23](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-23)

For replayed actions, verify expected intermediate interface state at each relevant step. If it differs, stop the replay and fall back to adaptive reasoning rather than continuing a stale macro. In an experimental conference-schedule replay, a filtering hiccup led to fallback; the predicates and missed-error rate were not specified. Repeatability and adaptation remain a tradeoff, not a solved reliability guarantee. [Source 24](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-24)

## Record gates and the historical action chain

Ask for a separate result for each instructed gate, rather than accepting one compressed checklist claim. This can expose omissions, especially with weaker instruction followers, but prompt-level logging is neither independent enforcement nor tamper-proof evidence. [Source 25](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-25)

An action receipt answers a broader historical question. Record the trigger and its identity, inherited state, proposal, applicable authority decision, actual arguments and attempts, and the external result or failure to confirm it. Preserve the actual inputs, model and configuration, output and reviewer action: a later rerun is not what happened then. An internal message tool accepting a request, for example, does not establish that a user saw the message; delivery and persistence can fail separately. The receipt is a proposed architectural contract, not a standard format or cryptographic proof. [Source 26](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-26) [Source 27](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-27) [Source 28](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-28) [Source 29](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-29)

Start an audit with one real path: identify its trigger, inherited state, authority, execution and surviving evidence. Trace each side effect through attempts and any idempotency information to the boundary the user cares about. This is an inspectable starting point, not a reliability assessment of the whole deployment. [Source 30](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-30)

## Bound triggers, recovery and changing goals

Specify when an unattended agent wakes—on an event or schedule—and the evidence window it should inspect. Monitor expected runs and silent failures separately from the quality of produced artifacts; a trigger is not completion. Three- or six-hour sweeps are examples, not optimal intervals. [Source 31](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-31) [Source 32](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-32)

Give external calls deadlines, cancellation and explicit terminal outcomes, and let recovery commands bypass the lane blocked by the operation they repair. Feed errors back into the workflow, cap retries and exploratory investigation by count or time, then validate, report or escalate. Select limits for the operation and its risks; a cited three-retry example is not a universal optimum. The incident motivating the blocked-lane proposal had no established exact cause. [Source 33](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-33) [Source 34](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-34) [Source 35](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-35) [Source 36](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-36)

After interruption, inspect existing work before starting over: a dirty working tree and passing tests are clues, not proof of completion. Saving progress outside a disposable runtime can enable resumption, but neither saved state nor retries establish exactly-once external effects. In the discussed generated-code setup, resuming inside a failed program remained an open problem. See [Running and resuming agent sessions](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-sessions-and-long-running-work.html) for session lifecycle. [Source 37](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-37) [Source 38](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-38) [Source 39](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-39)

Finally, allow the route to change when the user changes their goal: a cancellation conversation need not remain locked in its original branch. Re-establish the intended outcome and apply the same relevant controls and verification to the new route. This is a design argument, not a demonstrated improvement in satisfaction or safety. [Source 40](#agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence-source-40)

## Running and resuming agent sessions

Own session lifecycle, persistence and event execution; distinguish working-session state from curated organizational memory.

A long-running agent is not just a slow request. The client may disconnect, an execution container may fail, a tool may wait, and a later worker may need to continue. Design where the session’s state is held and who can recover it independently of where a model call happens.

## Separate session persistence from execution failure

If the harness and its execution sandbox share a container, losing that container can lose the session with it. One proposed design separates a stateless harness and sandboxed execution from an append-only session log, with credentials stored separately. A replacement harness can consult durable records rather than relying on the dead container’s memory. This is a vendor architecture proposal, not evidence of an independently verified security boundary or complete recovery. Access enforcement belongs to [Agent Authority, Isolation and Runtime Controls](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-authority-isolation-and-runtime-controls.html). [Source 1](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-1)

## Specify what survives interruption

Decide what identifies a session, what records its history and outstanding work, where that state is held, and how a replacement worker rehydrates it after interruption or inactivity. A managed runtime may provide compute without supplying every persistence and rehydration behavior an application needs: one team reports adding those pieces itself. Long-running evaluation workers face the same requirement to resume or respawn while preserving a consistent run, but the cited account provides no checkpoint format or recovery benchmark. [Source 2](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-2) [Source 3](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-3)

A log of events is not automatically an executable checkpoint: it may document what happened without preserving enough state to continue safely. Nor does a resumed worker imply that external actions were reversed. Specify and test the actual recovery contract; use [Managing agent task flow and action evidence](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence.html) for action evidence and operational recovery rather than treating session persistence as proof of either.

## Exchange events without making the client the worker

An event interface lets a client send user-message events and listen for agent events while execution has its own lifecycle. In a workshop chat application, the backend relays a server-sent event stream to the browser. Separating event storage from session mechanics also allows new recorded event types without tying all persistence changes to execution. Filter model and tool events for observation, but do not confuse an event feed with resumable state; the workshop’s longer-duration capability claims were not demonstrated as elapsed runs. [Source 4](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-4) [Source 5](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-5) [Source 6](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-6)

For shared chat, one proposed mapping assigns a session to each thread, identifies the sender in injected messages and provides an explicit reply tool. Separate agents and memory per channel may help when channel boundaries matter. Thread mapping is routing, not proof of authorization or tenant isolation; assess access separately. [Source 7](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-7)

## Preserve useful working context

An unattended run needs the task goal, prior attempts and relevant tradeoffs, but indiscriminately adding telemetry can leave both noise and critical evidence gaps. One practitioner prepares an overnight run with business context and clarification before leaving it unattended; another describes investigations with too much low-value context and missing essential logs. Choose context by relevance and identify what is unavailable, rather than simply maximizing or minimizing its size. [Source 8](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-8) [Source 9](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-9)

Compaction makes room in the model’s working window but can discard details needed later. A deliberately naive demonstration retained the system prompt, task and last two messages while dropping intervening history; that does not establish preservation of working state. An append-only original log offers a possible way to retrieve earlier events after compaction, provided retrieval, selection and access controls work. A provider reports ten-hour sessions using compaction but gives no compaction-quality measurement or evidence of year-long continuous operation. [Source 10](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-10) [Source 11](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-11) [Source 12](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-12)

Working context is selected material for this session; a retained event log is its historical record; an executable checkpoint must support continuation; curated organizational memory serves later work. These are different forms of custody and cannot be substituted merely because each contains text. For curation see [Maintaining agent context, memory and knowledge](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/reliable-agent-context-and-memory.html).

## Steer a waiting session without assuming rewind

A corrective user-message event can be queued to influence future work; it does not undo earlier actions or roll execution back. In one discussed product, ordinary messages can queue while a model works, but a custom-tool wait blocks message injection and returns HTTP 400 to preserve ordering. A proposed coordinator delegates that blocking work to a subagent so the main thread stays responsive; the discussion does not validate all races. Forking or rewind was a requested roadmap feature, not demonstrated recovery. Clients need to represent the waiting state and handle the product’s actual ordering semantics. [Source 13](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-13) [Source 14](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-14) [Source 15](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-15)

## Queue compute separately from choosing execution placement

For hours-long training, an agent can prepare code and parameters, submit the actual run to a separate compute queue, poll for results and resume analysis when it finishes. This avoids holding one conversational turn open for the whole job. The demonstrated queue does not establish scheduling guarantees, fault tolerance or recovery; the session still needs a way to remember the job and interpret its eventual result. [Source 16](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-16)

A remote sandbox answers a different question: where should the agent workflow execute? A speaker recommends getting a debugging loop working locally before moving it to scheduled or event-triggered sandbox execution. Remote placement can let work continue after a laptop closes and permits different resource choices, but it does not itself provide durable session state. Hosted or on-premises security, synchronization and portability claims in these accounts are not independent validation. [Source 17](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-17) [Source 18](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-18) [Source 19](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-19)

## Schedule invocations and version their resources

In one product, a deployment combines an agent definition, schedule, initial messages and optional resources such as repositories or memory stores. Each scheduled invocation starts a session; an on-demand invocation is also possible. This differs from keeping one session open indefinitely, and the deployment is not a frozen snapshot of every referenced agent. Some workshop runs failed, so scheduling does not guarantee execution. [Source 20](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-20)

The same speakers describe storing durable agent resource definitions as versioned YAML and using a CLI and API from CI/CD to update them. Versioned configuration helps reconstruct intended changes, but does not preserve a running session or prove which mutable referenced resources were used at invocation. The workshop does not verify all resource types or provide a complete deployment recipe. [Source 21](#agent-sessions-and-long-running-work-source-21)

For selecting triggers, evidence windows and monitoring missing runs, see [Managing agent task flow and action evidence](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence.html).

[Watch original](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QSeaZ6qHyXs) · [Transcript lines](https://github.com/flaviusapop/ai-engineer-evals/blob/main/transcripts/QSeaZ6qHyXs.md#L18-L21)

## Choosing agent delegation and coordination

Own topology, specialist coordination and capacity tradeoffs; link model portfolio selection to routing-and-deployment.

Splitting work across agents is useful only when the resulting pieces can be coordinated and their results put back together. Begin with the work, not a desired agent count: identify which parts are checkable, what depends on what, and who has capacity to inspect the combined result.

## Select checkable nodes and retain takeover

A whole workflow need not have one autonomy setting. Screen each proposed node: is its output bounded, traceable and checkable against the relevant rules? Can an accountable person inspect the result, stop the run and take over when it fails? An agent might assemble evidence for a lending decision while the difficult, policy-sensitive final decision remains human-driven. These are qualitative screening questions, not an authorization score. [Source 1](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-1)

A proposed stop-and-resume hook returns control to a person when an evaluator detects a condition, accepts a message and continues. Start with close expert review; only reduce routine review when task-specific evidence meets an explicitly chosen policy, while keeping a way to investigate and intervene. The cited staged approach does not specify thresholds or sampling rates. An agent's explanation can aid inspection but can itself be wrong. [Risk-based autonomy](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/risk-based-safety-and-staged-autonomy.html) and [runtime enforcement](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-authority-isolation-and-runtime-controls.html) address distinct decisions. [Source 2](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-2) [Source 3](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-3) [Source 4](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-4)

## Start with a reliable loop; split only for a real boundary

First make one agent loop work on the task. Add a role when it has a distinct job, context, tool set or organizational owner that warrants a handoff. In one diagnostic case, a single prompt had to handle troubleshooting, formatting and failure patterns; improving instructions for one behavior reportedly hurt another. The team separated focused prompts and tool subsets, making roles easier to maintain and test. This is a case observation, not a controlled demonstration that specialists always outperform a single agent. [Source 5](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-5) [Source 6](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-6) [Source 7](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-7)

A stage boundary makes it easier to locate a failure, but sequential calls add latency and another place to fail. The same diagnostic team found its trial of a more rigid workflow brittle for open-ended troubleshooting; that experience does not rule out deterministic sequencing when the task requires it. Top-level ownership can remain serial while a worker runs bounded research tasks in parallel. A vendor describes such a design, but does not establish that its fresh-context handoffs improve performance in a controlled comparison. [Source 8](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-8) [Source 9](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-9) [Source 10](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-10)

## Choose topology by dependency and reconcile the whole task

A central orchestrator can distribute dependent work, retain a common view and provide an investigation point. Event choreography lets consumers respond to relevant events without a central round trip, which is attractive when their tasks do not depend on one another. Direct messages can avoid central coordination but fragment state: each participant may see a different version of the task. These are architectural tradeoffs, not measured universal latency or reliability results. Independence here means no execution dependency; it does **not** imply statistically independent model errors. [Source 11](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-11) [Source 12](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-12)

A model-selected topology permits adaptation to the problem; a provider favors it, but supplies no comparison protocol. Conversely, a team supporting many integrations used reference patterns to limit variation. A middle choice gives agents discretion over decomposition while retaining explicit bookkeeping and checks for unresolved work. Compare these choices on the actual task and support burden, not on a presumed winner. [Source 13](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-13) [Source 14](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-14) [Source 15](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-15)

Send each specialist the goal, relevant shared constraints and the context needed for its assignment; configuration inheritance is not necessarily conversation inheritance. One described subagent inherited prompts and tool schemas but not the parent transcript. Preserve shared state and return a structured account of completed and unfinished work, evidence and issues, so the coordinator can identify gaps; see [task handoffs](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-task-flow-and-action-evidence.html) for action evidence. [Source 16](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-16) [Source 17](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-17)

For example, independently reasonable flight and hotel choices may refer to incompatible destinations. Reconciliation must compare outputs against the **whole** objective and constraints, not merely concatenate them. A judge can flag inconsistency, but it is not proof that every cross-cutting architectural or security tradeoff was considered; a reviewer may still need to challenge missing context. [Source 18](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-18) [Source 19](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-19)

## Gate specialist participation and investigate competing hypotheses

A narrow specialist need not write a full response every time. In a reported clinical architecture, specialists first decide whether their area is relevant; those with nothing to contribute short-circuit, while relevant outputs go to the main conversation model. This can avoid needless contributions, but the gate can miss a relevant issue. The vendor account does not establish reliability or a measured latency benefit; specialist participation is not approval or independent proof. [Source 20](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-20)

Diagnosis calls for a different pattern. In a reported job-troubleshooting system, triage examines the lifecycle, proposes competing failure hypotheses and sends each to parallel evidence researchers. A supervisor selects a confidence-scored explanation; a separate healer retrieves possible remedies from runbooks, and a report is assembled. This preserves the distinction between evidence for a cause and guidance for responding to it. The scores were not shown calibrated: the highest score is not proof of causality, and a plausible runbook remedy does not prove the diagnosis. [Source 21](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-21)

## Budget the human and validation bottleneck

More parallel agents create more routing, review and integration decisions for people. Measure ready-to-submit delay and retries, CI and review queues, integration and rework, alongside product quality and human interventions. A green check or high PR count is not itself delivered quality. Fix flaky tests and consider incremental builds, caching or sharding where CI is the constraint; preserve time for people to interpret monitoring signals as well as review changes. [Source 22](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-22) [Source 23](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-23) [Source 24](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-24) [Source 25](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-25)

Backpressure ties generation to available review. In one workflow, a scheduled loop checks for an existing labeled PR before starting and stops if one remains open. That limits outstanding work **per labeled loop**, not across the team. The same practitioner suggests bounded batches or distributing separate PRs among reviewers when capacity allows; reviewer fan-out requires a deliberate change to the one-open-PR rule. Larger PRs may amortize CI waits but make careful review harder. Prioritize a few evidence-rich findings rather than flooding reviewers, and measure whether review and quality actually keep up. [Source 26](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-26) [Source 27](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-27) [Source 28](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-28) [Source 29](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-29)

## Separate coordination planes and check the environment

An execution plane performs the user's work. One proposed evaluation control plane instead collects telemetry, runs simulations and coordinates human review; the talk does not specify its intervention mechanisms. A different vendor architecture uses a PR-validation control plane to coordinate workflow state, alongside an agent runtime and model routing. These planes have different jobs: neither label proves a safety guarantee or quality gain. For monitoring and ownership, see [Monitoring production quality and improvement](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/production-evaluation-and-monitoring.html) and [Evaluation infrastructure and team ownership](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/evaluation-platform-and-team-ownership.html). [Source 30](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-30) [Source 31](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-31)

Before porting a design, test the actual harness for subagent support, permissions, user interaction, hooks and wakeup on task completion. Identical instruction files do not ensure identical execution. An experimental browser-feedback bridge used a poller that completed after a user annotation, allowing the agent to consume the event; the speaker noted remaining problems and preferred a first-party integration. Report unsupported or degraded behavior rather than assuming the bridge works everywhere. These capability descriptions were made at talk time, not guarantees about current products. [Session lifecycle](https://flaviusapop.github.io/ai-engineer-evals/wiki/articles/agent-sessions-and-long-running-work.html) and runtime authorization remain separate concerns. [Source 32](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-32) [Source 33](#agent-delegation-and-coordination-source-33)
